title: Cocartesian cancellation and initiality of lifts
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces and initial objects from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations and horn-cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories. Given a $2$-simplex with edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$, and $w:x\to z$, if $u$ is $p$-cocartesian, then $v$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if $w$ is $p$-cocartesian. Every degenerate edge is $p$-cocartesian. For $x\in E$ and an edge $f:p(x)\to b$, form
$$L(x,f)=E_{x/}\times_{B_{p(x)/}}\{f\}.$$
Here $(E_{x/})_n$ consists of maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to E$ with first vertex $x$, with operators induced on the last $n+1$ vertices while keeping the first vertex fixed, and $\{f\}$ is the constant vertex simplicial subset in the corresponding coslice of $B$. Then $L(x,f)$ is a quasicategory, and every $p$-cocartesian lift $x\to y$ of $f$ is initial in $L(x,f)$. A morphism from this lift to another lift $x\to y'$ is a map $y\to y'$ over $1_b$ together with its commuting triangle and all higher data. In particular the universal comparison from one initial lift to another is an equivalence in this lift category; forgetting the triangle gives the corresponding equivalence of targets in $E_b$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7, Corollary 2.4.1.6 and Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category duals; coslice fibers are the slice models used in the latter remark. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text:
Fix a test vertex $t$ of $E$. The mapping-space criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] gives the squares whose upper row is
$$\operatorname{Map}_E(z,t)\xrightarrow{v^*}\operatorname{Map}_E(y,t)\xrightarrow{u^*}\operatorname{Map}_E(x,t),$$
with the corresponding row in $B$ below it. The square on the RIGHT is the square for $u$, and is a homotopy pullback by hypothesis. Precomposition with $w$ is homotopic to $u^*v^*$ by associativity and the component dependence in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]: the given triangle gives $[w]=[v][u]$. The compatibility with $p$ is checked on the displayed composition spans, rather than only on components. Write $P_U$ and $P_V$ for applying $p$ to the arrow spaces $U$ and triangle spaces $V$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Restriction of simplices gives the strict equations $\theta_B P_V=(P_U\times P_U)\theta_E$ and $\ell_B P_V=P_U\ell_E$, and [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] gives $P_Uj_E=j_BP_M$ on the right-pinched spaces. Thus the comparison obtained by inverting $\theta$ is compatible with $p$: for homotopy inverses $q_E,q_B$, the homotopy is the explicit chain $q_B(P_U\times P_U)\simeq q_B(P_U\times P_U)\theta_Eq_E=q_B\theta_BP_Vq_E\simeq P_Vq_E$. Use these homotopies with the associativity and unit comparisons of the cited composition class. The supplied triangle, and its image under $p$, specify the comparison from the pasted top row to precomposition by $w$ and its corresponding bottom comparison. Retain this comparison of the whole two-row diagram, including the commutation homotopies; the outer rectangle is therefore the coherent mapping square for $w$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] with right square the square for $u$ and left square the square for $v$. It gives that the square for $v$ is a homotopy pullback if and only if the square for $w$ is. This applies for every $t$; the mapping-space criterion in both directions proves the asserted cancellation.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7, opposite-category dual; mapping-space proof by homotopy-pullback pasting.

proof.text: Let $e=s_0x:x\to x$ be a degenerate edge of $E$. It is an equivalence edge in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: its inverse is $e$ itself, and the degenerate $2$-simplex $s_0s_0x$, whose three edges are all $e$, witnesses both inverse equations. Let $n\geq2$, let $\beta:\Delta^n\to B$, and let $a:\Lambda_0^n\to E$ satisfy $pa=\beta|_{\Lambda_0^n}$ and $a|_{[0,1]}=e$. Since $p$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] applies to this equivalence edge and gives $\widetilde\beta:\Delta^n\to E$ with $\widetilde\beta|_{\Lambda_0^n}=a$ and $p\widetilde\beta=\beta$. This is exactly the horn condition defining a $p$-cocartesian edge in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], for every $n\geq2$. No mapping-space or homotopy-invariance argument is needed, and empty mapping spaces cause no special case.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.1.6, opposite-category dual (identity edges are cocartesian).

proof.text: Here is the inner-horn calculation for the displayed coslices, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A lifting problem for $\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, in $E_{x/}\to B_{p(x)/}$ is a map from the coned horn $\Delta^0\star\Lambda_i^n$ to $E$, over the prescribed $(n+1)$-simplex of $B$, with cone vertex $x$. First fill its last-vertices horn $\Lambda_i^n$ in $E$ over the last-vertices face of that base simplex, using $p$. Adjoining this face to the coned horn gives exactly $\Lambda_{i+1}^{n+1}$: the face $d_0$ is the face just adjoined, and all other faces except $d_{i+1}$ were prescribed. Since $0<i+1<n+1$, a second inner-horn lift along $p$ gives the required coslice simplex. Thus the coslice map is an inner fibration. An inner horn in its degreewise fiber over $f$ is a lifting problem with the constant base simplex at $f$, so its lift stays in that fiber. This proves that the displayed $L(x,f)$ is a quasicategory. The coned horn is simply the union of the faces specified above; no join theorem is needed. The degreewise pullback retains the entire base simplex, triangles, and higher data.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.1, fixed-source specialization; explicit two-inner-horn calculation.

proof.text: Let $\ell:x\to y$ be a cocartesian lift of $f$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to the inner fibration $L(x,f)\to\Delta^0$ (Step 3), and vertex $\ell$. Its $p$-initial predicate here says exactly that every $\operatorname{Map}_{L(x,f)}(\ell,g)$ is contractible, because the mapping spaces of $\Delta^0$ are points. To verify its boundary criterion, take $n>0$ and $a:\partial\Delta^n\to L(x,f)$ with $a(0)=\ell$. Unwinding the coslice gives the coned boundary $\Delta^0\star\partial\Delta^n=\Lambda_0^{n+1}\to E$, whose edge $01$ is $\ell$. The prescribed base simplex is the composite $\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^1\xrightarrow{f}B$ sending vertex $0$ to $0$ and every later vertex to $1$. Cocartesianness, defined in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], fills this outer horn over exactly that base simplex, since $n+1\geq2$. The filler is precisely an extension $\Delta^n\to L(x,f)$ of $a$. Thus every required boundary extends and the cited criterion proves initiality. For $n=1$ this is the triangle factoring any other lift through $\ell$; the higher dimensions give all compatibility data.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category dual, expanded directly from the horn definition using the boundary criterion.

proof.text: Fix an initial lift, so that the initial-object subcategory is nonempty. By the initial-object clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the full subcategory of initial objects of the quasicategory $L(x,f)$ is a contractible Kan complex. For completeness every edge $h:a\to b$ in this Kan subcategory is an equivalence by the horn definitions: fill $\Lambda_0^2$ with edges $01=h$, $02=1_a$ to get $g:b\to a$ and the triangle $(h,g,1_a)$. Fill $\Lambda_0^3$ on vertices $(a,b,a,b)$ with faces $d_3=(h,g,1_a)$, $d_1=(1_a,h,h)$, and $d_2=(h,1_b,h)$, the last two degenerate; its $d_0$ is $(g,h,1_b)$. These are the two inverse witnesses. Thus every comparison between initial lifts is an equivalence in $L(x,f)$, with its triangle and higher data retained. The strict fiber $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn in it is an inner horn in $E$ over a constant simplex, and the inner-fibration lift stays in the fiber. The forgetful map $L(x,f)\to E_b$ is simplicial; it carries the inverse and the two inverse-triangle witnesses of an equivalence to corresponding witnesses, so it carries this comparison to an equivalence of targets. The description of a morphism as a target map over $1_b$ with its commuting triangle is exactly the degreewise pullback definition of $L(x,f)$.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category dual; contractibility of the space of initial lifts and comparison equivalences.

split_report.summary: Five proof steps give cancellation with the right-square hypothesis correctly oriented, degenerate edges via units, coslice inner fibrancy by two explicit inner-horn lifts, initiality by the existing relative-initial boundary criterion and the cocartesian outer horn, and comparison equivalences by initial-object contractibility. Retained only the non-elementary generic homotopy-pullback pasting auxiliary; repaired its ancestry, node metadata and logged search records. No item statement change. Second reading makes the base compatibility of the composition spans explicit, cites naturality of the pinch comparison, and makes nonemptiness in the initial-object theorem explicit. Maintainer reader FIX: Step 2 now derives cocartesianness of degenerate edges directly from the horn definition and the equivalence outer-horn lifting node, replacing an argument marked elementary that relied on unstated homotopy invariance of path pullbacks under homotopic maps.
split_report.blueprint: The item realizes the inherited prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph input for cocartesian cancellation and initial lifts, as identified in blueprint.from.place.

tool_uses.why: Step 5 uses exactly its theorem that the full subcategory of initial objects of any quasicategory, if nonempty, is a contractible Kan complex. This is generic infinity-category calculus, not a replacement for the unit route; no node of this unit states it.

Step 2 uses exactly its statement that an inner fibration of quasicategories fills every Lambda_0^n horn (n>=2) whose edge 01 is an equivalence edge, over the prescribed base simplex; a degenerate edge is such an edge. This is the generic Joyal outer-horn lifting tool of sk-prop-sf-cbc; no node of this unit states it, and it replaces the earlier homotopy-invariance argument through the mapping criterion that had been marked elementary.
